issues.title: Fix readinto type hint to accept memoryview for BufferedReader compatibility
issues.body:
## Summary

- Fixes `BaseHTTPResponse.readinto()` type annotation from `bytearray` to `bytearray | memoryview[int]`, matching the `io.RawIOBase.readinto` contract
- Adds a test exercising `readinto` with both `memoryview` and `bytearray` arguments
- The runtime implementation already handled both types correctly; this is purely a type annotation fix

## Motivation

Wrapping an `HTTPResponse` in `io.BufferedReader` causes mypy to emit a `[type-var]` error because `BufferedReader` expects its argument to satisfy the `_BufferedReaderStream` protocol, which requires `readinto(self, memoryview[int], /) -> int | None`. The current annotation only accepts `bytearray`.

```
error: Argument 1 to "BufferedReader" has incompatible type "HTTPResponse"; expected "_BufferedReaderStream"  [arg-type]
note: Following member(s) of "HTTPResponse" have conflicts:
note:     Expected:
note:         def readinto(self, memoryview[int], /) -> int | None
note:     Got:
note:         def readinto(self, b: bytearray) -> int
```

Closes #3764

## Test plan

- [x] New test `test_readinto_with_memoryview` covers `readinto` with `memoryview`, `bytearray`, and empty-read cases
- [x] All 185 existing tests in `test/test_response.py` continue to pass

The inputs we're putting in the test expressly violate the [typing contract](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/e765696ca0c3421bb5763e4b944d5c1bcca2e84a/Lib/typing.py#L3555-L3565) (and I think this is the first case of this in ~10 years of the code existing). Whether the object can support seek(), it should implement it in some form per [BaseIO](https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.IOBase.seek). Is there more info on how this was encountered?

Sorry, I thought I had put a link in the initial issue - but I hadn't. Background: - https://github.com/getsentry/objectstore/pull/329 - https://github.com/indygreg/python-zstandard/pull/287 So this arose out the combination of: - `getsentry/objectstore` passing a stream from `indygreg/python-zstandard` to `urllib3/urllib3` - `indygreg/python-zstandard` incorrectly implementing the interface - `urllib3/urllib3` retrying the request and attempting to rewind the body - `urllib3/urllib3` correctly throwing an error - but that error being quite confusing. issues.title: Fix _ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname overriding factory-created context's verify_mode
issues.body:
## Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  `_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname()` in `connection.py` creates an SSL context via                                                                                                                                                                       
  `create_urllib3_context()` (passing `cert_reqs`), then unconditionally overrides it:                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
      context.verify_mode = resolve_cert_reqs(cert_reqs)                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  This is correct for caller-supplied `ssl_context` (the `else` branch). But it also                                                                                                                                                                          
  runs when `default_ssl_context = True`, silently undoing whatever the factory configured.                                                                                                                                                                   
  The factory already received `cert_reqs` and applied it.                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Guard with `if not default_ssl_context:` so it only applies to caller-supplied contexts.                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Impact                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Any patch to `create_urllib3_context` that sets `verify_mode` is silently overridden.                                                                                                                                                                       
  Affects enterprise users behind SSL-intercepting proxies (Zscaler, Cisco Umbrella, etc.)                                                                                                                                                                    
  whose corporate CA certs predate strict RFC 5280 Basic Constraints compliance — they                                                                                                                                                                        
  cannot add their CA to the trust chain and must disable Python-level verification,                                                                                                                                                                          
  which this bug prevents.                        



Related issues #3614 and #3665 describe users hitting similar SSL failures with enterprise and Kubernetes CA certs in Python 3.13. Customizing the SSLContext was suggested as a workaround in both threads, this fix ensures that approach works consistently, as currently any factory-level customization is silently overridden before the connection is made.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  nuclearpidgeon's workaround in #3665 (passing a manually-constructed ssl_context directly) works precisely because caller-supplied contexts hit the else branch. This fix extends that capability to factory-created contexts, allowing application-level patches to create_urllib3_context to take effect without requiring every caller to construct and pass their own context.


 ## Historical context  
Tracing the git history suggests this regression was introduced in ea96fde ("Change proxy TLS flow to match destination TLS flow", Jan 2022). Prior to that commit, context was always self.ssl_context, a pre-existing connection-level context with no factory path, so applying cert_reqs unconditionally was correct. When _ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname was extracted and the create_urllib3_context factory branch was added, the override line was transplanted from the old connect() method where context was always a pre-existing self.ssl_context — correct there, but not reconciled with the newly introduced factory branch in the same commit, causing it to also run on factory-created contexts.

  I considered moving the line into the else branch instead, but opted for the if not default_ssl_context: guard to make the intent explicit: the factory owns the configuration of its own context, and the override only applies when the caller supplies their own. Happy to adjust if the maintainers prefer a different approach.

issues.body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7.0.0 to 8.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to false.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

issues.title: SOCKS proxy URIs with percent-encoded userinfo do not work
issues.body:
### Subject

A SOCKS proxy URI userinfo subcomponent containing percent encoded values (e.g. `socks5h://user:%70ass@host:1080`) will not have the username and password be percent decoded or unquoted before they're passed to the proxy server for authentication.

### Environment

```
OS: Linux-6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-x86_64-with-glibc2.36
Python: 3.13.0
urllib3: 2.6.3
```

### Steps to Reproduce

I ran into this problem with a password containing a delimiter character that needed to be percent encoded to have the proxy URI correctly parsed.  Despite fixing the encoding, authentication failed.  As a synthetic test, one can percent encode any username or password character from a case that works and it will fail.

```python
import urllib3
p = 'socks5h://user:pass@host:1080'
spm = urllib3.contrib.socks.SOCKSProxyManager(proxy_url=p)
spm.request('GET', 'https://httpbin.org/ip').data
# suppose this works, now replace a character in the username or password with the percent encoded equivalent:
p = 'socks5h://user:%70ass@host:1080'
spm = urllib3.contrib.socks.SOCKSProxyManager(proxy_url=p)
spm.request('GET', 'https://httpbin.org/ip').data
# this should fail with: socks.SOCKS5AuthError: SOCKS5 authentication failed
```

### Expected Behavior

Pass percent decoded or unquoted username and password values to the proxy for authentication.

### Actual Behavior

Percent encoded usernames and passwords are presented to the proxy causing authentication failures.

### Additional Notes

While exploring this issue I convinced myself that it's reasonable for the parse_uri function and the Uri object to not hold percent decoded values, because they only break the URI down as far as subcomponents.  I would think differently if, like urllib's urlsplit function, there were accessors for username and password directly.

I believe the problem lies in the [SOCKSProxyManager](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/2.6.3/src/urllib3/contrib/socks.py#L196-L198):

```python
        parsed = parse_url(proxy_url)

        if username is None and password is None and parsed.auth is not None:
            split = parsed.auth.split(":")
            if len(split) == 2:
                username, password = split
```

After the username and password no longer have the semantics of the URI userinfo subcomponent, they should be percent decoded or unquoted for use in the rest of the application.  The ready example is "how does cURL handle this?" which is [here](https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/curl-8_18_0/lib/setopt.c#L2006-L2028):

```c
    /* URL decode the components */
    if(!result && u) {
      Curl_safefree(s->str[STRING_PROXYUSERNAME]);
      result = Curl_urldecode(u, 0, &s->str[STRING_PROXYUSERNAME], NULL,
                              REJECT_ZERO);
    }
    if(!result && p) {
      Curl_safefree(s->str[STRING_PROXYPASSWORD]);
      result = Curl_urldecode(p, 0, &s->str[STRING_PROXYPASSWORD], NULL,
                              REJECT_ZERO);
    }
```

I also tested using requests v2.32.5 which works, and uses urllib3, [but manually configures the SOCKSProxyManager username and password](https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/v2.32.5/src/requests/adapters.py#L256-L266) instead of relying on parsing the proxy_url:

```python
        elif proxy.lower().startswith("socks"):
            username, password = get_auth_from_url(proxy)
            manager = self.proxy_manager[proxy] = SOCKSProxyManager(
                proxy,
                username=username,
                password=password,
                num_pools=self._pool_connections,
                maxsize=self._pool_maxsize,
                block=self._pool_block,
                **proxy_kwargs,
            )
```

The [get_auth_from_url](https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/v2.32.5/src/requests/utils.py#L1017) utility performs the percent decode here.

issues.title: Fix proxy_ssl_context ignored for HTTPS forwarding proxies (#2577)
issues.body:
Found this while debugging SSL issues behind a corporate proxy in #3782. In forwarding mode there's only one TLS handshake and it was always using the destination ssl_context instead of the proxy one. Tunneling already worked because it has a dedicated _connect_tls_proxy() call. 

Fix is a 4-line branch in connect() to pick the right context. Also added ValueError when ssl_context and use_forwarding_for_https=True are both set, per the issue spec.


Fixes #2577.



## Root cause

The tunneling path (`proxy_is_tunneling`) was already handled correctly by `_connect_tls_proxy()`, which explicitly uses `proxy_config.ssl_context`. The forwarding path, however, fell through to the shared `_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname` call that always passed `self.ssl_context`.

## History

The bug dates to 691679f7 (Sept 2020) when forwarding proxy support was first introduced — the forwarding path was added with `ssl_context=self.ssl_context` and never corrected.    

## Fix


```python
if self.proxy_is_forwarding and self.proxy_config is not None:
    tls_ssl_context = self.proxy_config.ssl_context
else:
    tls_ssl_context = self.ssl_context
```


## Tests

- Removed the `pytest.skip("Test is expected to fail due to urllib3/urllib3#2577")` guard in `test_proxy_https_target_tls_error` — that test now passes directly.
- Added `test_https_proxy_forwarding_uses_proxy_ssl_context` which verifies that an HTTPS forwarding proxy works correctly when only `proxy_ssl_context` is supplied (no `ca_certs` fallback).

issues.title: HTTPConnection does not respect HTTPConnection.default_socket_options
issues.body:
### Subject

Changing` HTTPConnection.default_socket_options` does nothing.
Creating a new `HTTPConnection` will always use the default value from the class definition and will ignore any changes done to the `HTTPConnection.default_socket_options`  value.



### Environment

Tested on multiple platforms, the bug was introduced in version `2.0.0` and is present in all versions since then
Tested on Ubuntu (bare metal) and alpine linux (docker).
The bug is in urllib3 so should appear on any platform.

### Steps to Reproduce

A very detailed explanation can be seen bellow a bit bellow

### Expected Behavior

When changing `HTTPConnection.default_socket_options`, it is expected that future any connection created after that will use the new defaults.

### Actual Behavior

The new connections ignore `HTTPConnection.default_socket_options`

---

on lines https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/main/src/urllib3/connection.py#L140-L142 in the `__init__` of the HTTPConnection class, `socket_options` has default value `default_socket_options`.
This value is evaluated when the class itself is created, NOT when an instance of the class is created.
This means that once the class definition is loaded, this value can't be changed.
Changing `HTTPConnection.default_socket_options` does not change the already evaluated default value for `socket_options`

Here is a simple code snippet that demonstrates the issue , show what exactly is broken with a simplified `Test` class and also shows a hacky workaround that still allows to change the defaults.
```
from urllib3.connection import HTTPConnection, HTTPSConnection
import socket

class Test:
    """A simple test class to demonstrate the issue with default arguments being evaluated at function definition time."""

    default_test_conf:str= "default_value"
    test_conf: str | None
    def __init__(self, *, test_conf: None | str = default_test_conf):
        print (f"Initializing Test with test_conf: {test_conf}")
        print (f"Actual default test conf: {Test.default_test_conf}")
        self.test_conf = test_conf

print(f"Demonstrating the issue with HTTPConnection default_socket_options and a workaround by modifying the __kwdefaults__ of HTTPConnection.__init__ and HTTPSConnection.__init__\n")

print ("At this point the default for socket_options is already set")
print(f"HTTPConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options']: {HTTPConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options']}")

# we will now try to modify the defaults
HTTPConnection.default_socket_options = HTTPConnection.default_socket_options + [
    (socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_KEEPALIVE, 1),
    (socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_KEEPIDLE, 1),
    (socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_KEEPINTVL, 5),
    (socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_KEEPCNT, 5),
]

# passing socket_options explicitly should override the default_socket_options, works as expected
con: HTTPConnection = HTTPConnection('example.com', 80, socket_options=HTTPConnection.default_socket_options)
print(f"con.default_socket_options: {HTTPConnection.default_socket_options}")
print(f"con.socket_options: {con.socket_options}")

# when not passing socket_options should use the default_socket_options, does not work as expected
# con2.socket_options has the default socket options, not the modified default_socket_options with keepalive options, which is unexpected
con2: HTTPConnection = HTTPConnection('example.com', 80)
print(f"con2.default_socket_options: {HTTPConnection.default_socket_options}")
print(f"con2.socket_options: {con2.socket_options}")

# the problem is that HTTPConnection.__init__ has socket_options as a default argument, which is evaluated at function definition time, so it does not see the modified default_socket_options when it is defined
# here you can see that the default value for socket_options in HTTPConnection is the original default_socket_options, not the modified one with keepalive options
# the same is true for HTTPSConnection
print(f"HTTPConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options']: {HTTPConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options']}")
print(f"HTTPSConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options']: {HTTPSConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options']}")

# we can show that modifying the "HTTPConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options']" will actually change the default socket options used by HTTPConnection when socket_options is not passed explicitly, which is the workaround for this issue
HTTPConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options'] = HTTPConnection.default_socket_options
HTTPSConnection.__init__.__kwdefaults__['socket_options'] = HTTPSConnection.default_socket_options
con3: HTTPConnection = HTTPConnection('example.com', 80)
print(f"con3.default_socket_options: {HTTPConnection.default_socket_options}")
print(f"con3.socket_options: {con3.socket_options}")

# here is just a very simplified test to show the behavior explained above with a custom class and a default argument that is evaluated at function definition time, which is similar to the socket_options case in HTTPConnection

print("\n\nTesting custom class with default argument evaluated at function definition time:\n")
a = Test()
print(f"a.default_test_conf: {Test.default_test_conf}")
print(f"a.test_conf: {a.test_conf}")

Test.default_test_conf = "new_default_value"
b = Test()
print(f"b.default_test_conf: {Test.default_test_conf}")
print(f"b.test_conf: {b.test_conf}")

print(f"Test.__init__.__kwdefaults__['test_conf']: {Test.__init__.__kwdefaults__['test_conf']}")
Test.__init__.__kwdefaults__["test_conf"] = "another_default_value"
c = Test()
print(f"c.default_test_conf: {Test.default_test_conf}")
print(f"c.test_conf: {c.test_conf}")
```

issues.title: `HTTPResponse.stream` can fall into infinite loop when `amt` is zero
issues.body:
### Subject

`HTTPResponse.stream` generator can safely handle the situation when amt is positive integer, negative integer and `None`. However, `amt=0` can lead to catastrophic infinite loop (while `HTTPResponse.read(0)` is legit). This behavior is implicit, not covered in docs and tests.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import urllib3

r = urllib3.request("GET", "https://example.com", preload_content=False)

for chunk in r.stream(0):
    print(chunk)
```

### Actual Behavior

Run into infinite loop

### Expected Behavior

Anything else (handled the same way as `None` / explicitly raise a ValueError / return with empty output, etc.)

issues.title: Handle HTTP/2 StreamReset and ConnectionTerminated events
issues.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have read the repository contribution guidelines.
- [x] I have manually tested the changes proposed in this pull request.
- [x] I have written new test cases for new code and/or updated existing tests for changes to existing code.
- [ ] I have updated the documentation.

## Reference to Existing Issue

Closes #3291.

## Description of Changes

`HTTP2Connection.getresponse()` handled successful response events but ignored `h2`'s `StreamReset` and `ConnectionTerminated` error events. That could leave the receive loop waiting for more socket data instead of raising a urllib3 error, and it could also leave a GOAWAYed connection reusable.

This change translates those event types into `ConnectionError`s, allows a fully buffered response to complete only when GOAWAY still covers the active stream via `last_stream_id`, and retires the connection afterward. It also avoids sending a second local GOAWAY when the peer has already terminated the connection.

issues.title: Fix late-bound default_socket_options in HTTPConnection
issues.body:
### Summary
- Fixes a bug where `HTTPConnection.default_socket_options` changes were ignored because default arguments were bound at function definition time.
- Changed the default value of `socket_options` to `None` in both `HTTPConnection` and `HTTPSConnection`, evaluating it at runtime instead.

### Motivation
In Python, default arguments are evaluated only once at definition time. Since `socket_options` was defaulting to the class-level `default_socket_options` list directly, any subsequent changes to the class variable were not picked up by new connection instances. This fix ensures dynamic evaluation.

### Test plan
- Added `test_HTTPConnection_respects_default_socket_options_change` to verify that modifying the class variable affects new instances.
- Added a similar test for `HTTPSConnection`.
- Verified with `nox -rs test-3.13`.

Closes #3789

issues.title: fix: prevent infinite loop in HTTPResponse.stream when amt=0
issues.body:
<!---
Thanks for your contribution! ♥️

If this is your first PR to urllib3 please review the Contributing Guide:
https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contributing.html

Adhering to the Contributing Guide means we can review, merge, and release your change faster! :)
--->

Fixes #3793

When `amt=0` is passed to `HTTPResponse.stream()`, `read(amt=0)` returns `b""`, which is falsy and never yielded, but the file pointer remains open. This causes the while loop to spin indefinitely.

This adds an early return when `amt` is not None and `<= 0`, consistent with how `read(0)` returns immediately with `b""`.

A test is included to verify the fix.

Added the changelog entry in `changelog/3793.bugfix.rst` as requested. Thanks for the pointer!
@nightcityblade please check other comments

Thanks for the review! You're right — negative numbers are already handled correctly in `read_chunked` and `read`, so the extra guard was unnecessary. Removed it in the latest push. Only keeping the `amt=0` early return to prevent the infinite loop.

### Context

This came up while working on psf/requests#7272.

The `_TYPE_BODY` type alias currently allows `str` and `bytes` independently, and `Iterable[bytes]` for streaming bodies:

https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/0248277dd7ac0239204889ca991353ad3e3a1ddc/src/urllib3/_base_connection.py#L9

But `Iterable[str]` is handled correctly at runtime through two separate code paths and imo should be included in the type. This code path has been used by Requests for essentially its entire existence.

`body_to_chunks()` passes any iterable through as chunks:

https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/0248277dd7ac0239204889ca991353ad3e3a1ddc/src/urllib3/util/request.py#L248-L252

Then if it's a `str`, connection.py encodes each chunk to UTF-8 before sending:

https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/0248277dd7ac0239204889ca991353ad3e3a1ddc/src/urllib3/connection.py#L504-L510

What confirmed this was likely an oversight rather than intentional is urllib3 already documents this behavior. Both [HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen()](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/0248277dd7ac0239204889ca991353ad3e3a1ddc/src/urllib3/connectionpool.py#L407) and [_make_request()](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/0248277dd7ac0239204889ca991353ad3e3a1ddc/src/urllib3/connectionpool.py#L635) describe body as:

> an iterable of :class:`str`/:class:`bytes`, or a file-like object.

That documentation was added in 2020, I believe it's worked for the majority of urllib3's existence too. We even have tests exercising this behavior that are currently suppressed for type mismatches.

### Reproduction

```python
import urllib3

def string_body():
    yield "hello "
    yield "world"
   
pool = urllib3.HTTPConnectionPool("httpbin.org", 80)
pool.urlopen("POST", "/post", body=string_body())
```

### Suggested fix

```python
_TYPE_BODY = Union[bytes, IO[Any], Iterable[bytes | str], str]
```

Or `Iterable[bytes] | Iterable[str]` if you prefer to keep them separate.

### Contribution

~~I have the [code change](https://github.com/nateprewitt/urllib3/commit/d1ded1b0f73389882268e732a826303d803d8227) ready if we're in agreement. It looks like this technically got "regressed" in urllib3 2.x since it was the documented behavior for 1.x.~~ I just opened the PR since I don't think this is contentious: https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3799

issues.title: Fix SOCKS proxy auth failure with percent-encoded userinfo
issues.body:
## Summary

Fixes #3785.

SOCKS proxy URIs with percent-encoded userinfo (e.g. `socks5h://user:%70ass@host:1080`) fail authentication because the username and password extracted from `parsed.auth` are not percent-decoded before being sent to the proxy server.

- Added `urllib.parse.unquote()` calls to percent-decode the username and password after extracting them from the proxy URL's auth component in `SOCKSProxyManager.__init__`.
- Added an integration test `test_socks_with_percent_encoded_auth_in_url` that verifies SOCKS5 authentication succeeds when credentials are percent-encoded in the proxy URI.
- Added a towncrier changelog fragment.

This is consistent with how cURL handles proxy userinfo (it calls `Curl_urldecode` on the extracted username and password) and how the `requests` library works around this by manually calling `unquote` via `get_auth_from_url`.

## Test plan

- [x] New test `test_socks_with_percent_encoded_auth_in_url` passes (uses `socks5://us%65r:%70ass@host:port` and verifies authentication succeeds with decoded `user:pass`).
- [x] All existing SOCKS proxy tests continue to pass (20/20).

issues.title: parse_url doesn't %-decode user/password
issues.body:
### Subject

As far as I understand[^rfc], reserved characters need to %-encoded in URLs.

[^rfc]: [RFC 3986 section 3.2.1.](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-3.2.1): `userinfo    = *( unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ":" )`

So, if you have user "u{er" with password "pa}}word" for example.com, you would encode it as `http://u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword@example.com`. However, parse_url doesn't decode those parts:

```py
>>> import urllib3
>>> urllib3.util.parse_url("http://u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword@example.com").auth
'u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword'
```

Even worse, it encodes them for invalid URLs if you try to work around it:

```py
>>> urllib3.util.parse_url("http://u{er:pass}}word@example.com").auth
'u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword'
```

Therefore, if you use it to parse an URL pass `url.auth` into `make_headers(basic_auth=url.auth)`, you get a 401 and a downtime (ask me how I know).


### Environment

```
OS macOS-26.4-x86_64-i386-64bit-Mach-O
Python 3.14.3
OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026
urllib3 2.6.3
```

### Steps to Reproduce

See above.

### Expected Behavior

`urllib3.util.parse_url("http://u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword@example.com").auth` should return `u{er:pa}}word`.

`yarl` and `httpx.URL` get this right.

### Actual Behavior

It returns `u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword`

This behavior is shared by the stdlib and ada_url.

nodes.body:
See also #3785

I thought about approaching my bug report this way, but convinced myself that it was reasonable for urllib3 to not unquote the "auth" property value because it seems to represent the RFC named userinfo subcomponent and the library choosing not to present accessors for user and password avoids problems, for example, suppose the percent-encoded userinfo contains a colon, and the auth value is used but was unquoted internally, it's impossible for the caller to know which is the separator colon.

`parse_url()` returns a `Url` object, which is intended to preserve URL components in their parsed form.

For `userinfo`, RFC 3986 [requires ](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-3.2.1) reserved characters such as `{}` to be percent-encoded, so preserving and enriching the percent-encoded representation here appears consistent with that model.

As a result, `Url.auth` is not currently a decoded username/password value, and it is not well suited to be passed directly to `make_headers(basic_auth=...)` without additional handling.

I can see how that behavior would be confusing. This may be worth clarifying in the docs, or potentially revisiting the API to make the distinction between parsed URL credentials and decoded auth values more explicit.

issues.title: fix(parse_url): decode percent-encoded auth credentials
issues.body:
Fixes #4945

## Problem

`parse_url()` does not decode percent-encoded characters in the auth (userinfo) component of URLs. When a URL contains `http://u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword@example.com`, the `auth` property returns `u%7Ber:pass%7D%7Dword` instead of the decoded `u{er:pass}}word`.

This causes authentication failures when the parsed auth is passed to `make_headers(basic_auth=url.auth)`, as the server expects the actual credentials, not their percent-encoded form.

The behavior is inconsistent with other popular HTTP libraries like `yarl` and `httpx` which correctly decode auth components.

## Fix

- Added `from urllib.parse import unquote` import
- Changed the auth processing to decode percent-encoded characters using `unquote()` instead of re-encoding invalid characters with `_encode_invalid_chars()`

## Tests

- Added `test_parse_url_decodes_percent_encoded_auth` with 5 test cases covering:
  - Normal auth (no encoding needed)
  - Curly braces in auth (`%7B`, `%7D`)
  - `@` and `#` characters in auth (`%40`, `%23`)
  - Simple auth string
  - No auth present

nodes.body:
I would pose the following questions:

Should the Url.auth property, which appears to represent the RFC 3986 userinfo subcomponent, be presented with percent encoded values decoded?  This seems to obviously present a problem with username or password values that contain colons, preventing the user from accurately identifying either the username or password.

Should username and password properties be added to Url, that would be unquoted, to allow easier consumption of the underlying information with less ambiguity?

We added properties providing decoded auth in #5055.
`Url.auth` is not intended to provide the decoded auth.

Thanks for the contribution!

issues.title: Fix CRLF Injection in HTTP/1.1 putheader (CWE-93)
issues.body:
## Summary
Adds header value validation to prevent CRLF injection attacks in HTTP/1.1 connections.

## Vulnerability
CWE-93: CRLF Injection - urllib3 validates header NAMES but not VALUES in HTTP/1.1 connections, allowing HTTP Response Splitting attacks.

## Fix
- Added regex validation for control characters (CR, LF, NUL) in header values
- Matches the protection already present in HTTP/2 connections

## Files Changed
- `src/urllib3/connection.py`: Added header value validation in `putheader()`

## Testing
The fix properly blocks:
- `ValueError` for headers containing \r, \n, or \0
- Normal headers continue to work

## References
- CWE-93: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/93.html
- RFC 7230 Section 3.2.4

issues.title: Fix parsing behavior for ambiguous paths
issues.body:
## Overview

This PR is an attempt to address #3352. When a URI contains a path resembling a schemeless URI, urllib3 raises a `LocationParseError` in the `HTTPConnectionPool`. The existing code already treats all `/` prefixed URIs as paths via `_encode_target`, discarding the parse_url result entirely for these cases. The `parse_url` call was never
needed here and only causes problems when paths like //v:h get misinterpreted as a schemeless authority.

Removing this will also resolve the broken URL handling (#6711) that was added to Requests to work around this case.

## Proposed Change

We can shift the call order at the beginning of `urlopen` to skip these URIs without changing the current semantics. Anything that starts with a slash is inherently schemeless, so we set destination_scheme = None and encode the path directly. This matches the existing behavior but avoids the crash.

In the context of `connectionpool.urlopen()`, a `/` prefixed URI is always a path because `PoolManager` has already extracted the host, port, and scheme. The `//` prefix only looks like a schemeless authority in isolation.

If these _were_ for some reason schemeless authority URIs (//host/path), they were already broken at this layer. The existing code runs them through `_encode_target` as paths regardless. Given schemeless URIs are marked for deprecation, it seems sensible to leave the current behavior as it is.

nodes.body:
Thanks for the review, @illia-v! I'm not sure we actually have a behavior change here unless I'm missing something? The `parsed_url` is only used when it doesn't start with `/` and that was true in Jorge's PR as well. All this PR should do is prevent an unnecessary `parse_url` call where we weren't using the result anyway.

In the current code:

1. We parse `//example.com` as `scheme=None`, `host=example.com`, `path=/`. So our `destination_scheme` is None.
https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/166f66faa5ef23e255f654e8c6b66ad8590fe630/src/urllib3/connectionpool.py#L705-L706
2. Then we continue down to this block and because the `url` (not `parsed.url`) of `//example.com` starts with a `/`, it uses the original value. The parsed form isn't used today and won't be used in this PR either.
https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/166f66faa5ef23e255f654e8c6b66ad8590fe630/src/urllib3/connectionpool.py#L721-L725

The only change we're making in this PR is setting `destination_scheme` to `None` preemptively when we encounter a value starting with `/` because we know it can't have a scheme. I could leave the block on `721-725` alone, we'd just have two `if url.startswith("/")` blocks which felt redundant.

issues.title: Fix infinite loop in HTTPResponse.stream() when amt=0
issues.body:
## Problem

`HTTPResponse.stream(amt=0)` causes an infinite loop because `read(amt=0)` returns empty bytes without advancing the file position, and the while loop's `not is_fp_closed(self._fp)` condition never becomes false.

```python
r = urllib3.request("GET", "https://example.com", preload_content=False)
for chunk in r.stream(0):  # 💥 infinite loop
    print(chunk)
```

## Root Cause

1. `stream(0)` calls `read(amt=0)` which returns `b""` (empty bytes)
2. The `if data:` check skips yielding (empty string is falsy)
3. The while loop condition `not is_fp_closed(self._fp)` remains True
4. Loop repeats forever

## Fix

Add a guard at the start of `stream()` that raises `ValueError` when `amt == 0`, consistent with how `read()` normalizes negative amounts to `None`.

Includes a test.

Closes #3793

First, create a custom repository property with the name github-codeql-disable-overlay and the type "True/false" in the organization's settings. issues.body:
Bumps [astral-sh/setup-uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv) from 7.2.0 to 8.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from astral-sh/setup-uv's releases.

v8.0.0 🌈 Immutable releases and secure tags

This is the first immutable release of setup-uv 🥳

All future releases are also immutable, if you want to know more about what this means checkout the docs.

This release also has two breaking changes

New format for manifest-file

The previously deprecated way of defining a custom version manifest to control which uv versions are available and where to download them from got removed. The functionality is still there but you have to use the new format.

No more major and minor tags

To increase security even more we will stop publishing minor tags. You won't be able to use @v8 or @v8.0 any longer. We do this because pinning to major releases opens up users to supply chain attacks like what happened to tj-actions.

[!TIP] Use the immutable tag as a version astral-sh/setup-uv@v8.0.0 Or even better the githash astral-sh/setup-uv@cec208311dfd045dd5311c1add060b2062131d57

issues.title: proxy_ssl_context is mutated when target uses cert_reqs='CERT_NONE'
issues.body:
## Summary

When using `ProxyManager` with an HTTPS proxy and `cert_reqs='CERT_NONE'` for the target, urllib3 mutates the caller-provided `proxy_ssl_context` by overwriting its `verify_mode` to `CERT_NONE`. The mutation is permanent - it persists on the context object across all subsequent connections made through that `ProxyManager`.

## Reproduction

```python
import ssl
import urllib3
from urllib3.util.ssl_ import create_urllib3_context

proxy_ssl_context = create_urllib3_context()
proxy_ssl_context.load_verify_locations("/path/to/proxy-ca.pem")
proxy_ssl_context.check_hostname = False
proxy_ssl_context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_REQUIRED

print(f"Before: {proxy_ssl_context.verify_mode}")  # CERT_REQUIRED (2)

pm = urllib3.ProxyManager(
    "https://proxy.example.com:8443",
    proxy_ssl_context=proxy_ssl_context,
    cert_reqs="CERT_NONE",
)
pm.request("GET", "https://target.example.com/")

print(f"After: {proxy_ssl_context.verify_mode}")  # CERT_NONE (0) - mutated!
```

## Root Cause

Two issues in `connection.py`:

1. **`_connect_tls_proxy()`** passes `self.cert_reqs` (the *target's* cert_reqs) to `_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname()` for the proxy TLS handshake. When the target has `cert_reqs='CERT_NONE'`, this value leaks into the proxy path.

2. **`_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname()`** unconditionally sets `context.verify_mode = resolve_cert_reqs(cert_reqs)` on line 937, even when `context` is a user-provided `ssl_context` rather than an internally-created one. Since `ProxyConfig` holds a reference to the user's context (not a copy), the mutation sticks.

## Expected Behavior

A user-provided `proxy_ssl_context` should never be modified by urllib3. The proxy TLS handshake should use the proxy context's own `verify_mode`, not the target connection's `cert_reqs`.

## Environment

- urllib3 `main` branch (confirmed on v2.6.4.dev20)
- Python 3.13+ (likely affects all supported versions)

issues.title: Fix proxy_ssl_context mutation when target uses cert_reqs='CERT_NONE'
issues.body:
_connect_tls_proxy() was passing the target connection's cert_reqs to _ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname(), which then unconditionally overwrote verify_mode on the user-provided proxy_ssl_context. This caused the proxy context to permanently inherit the target's CERT_NONE setting.

Two changes:
- _connect_tls_proxy() now derives cert_reqs from the proxy context's own verify_mode when a proxy_ssl_context is provided.
- _ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname() no longer mutates verify_mode on user-provided ssl_context objects.

Fixes #4961

issues.title: CS-2094: Python 3.7 compatibility
issues.body:
## Summary

- Replace walrus operators (`:=`) with explicit assignments and add `try/except` fallbacks for `importlib.metadata` and `typing.TypedDict` to support Python 3.7 runtime
- Replace build backend (`hatchling` + `hatch-vcs` + `setuptools-scm`, all requiring Python ≥3.8) with `setuptools<69` + `wheel`; hardcode version `2.6.3.1` in `[project]` and a new static `src/urllib3/_version.py`
- Fix PEP 639 `license = "MIT"` syntax (triggers setuptools 77+ upgrade, which requires Python ≥3.8); replace with `license = {text = "MIT"}`
- Lower `requires-python` to `>=3.7`; add conditional runtime dependencies on `typing_extensions` and `importlib_metadata` for Python <3.8

## Test plan

- [ ] Build sdist/wheel under Python 3.7 interpreter and confirm no build-time errors
- [ ] `import urllib3; urllib3.__version__` returns `"2.6.3.1"` on Python 3.7
- [ ] Run existing test suite on Python 3.7

Hi maintainers,

While checking which downstream branches still need CVE-2026-21441, I noticed `1.26.x` may still be vulnerable.

**Upstream fix**: [`8864ac407b`](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/commit/8864ac407bba8607950025e0979c4c69bc7abc7b) — *Merge commit from fork*

**What I checked**
1. Fetched the upstream fix diff via the GitHub commits API
2. Fetched each affected file on `1.26.x` HEAD via the contents API
3. Compared additive lines from the fix against the branch HEAD content

**Result**: 2 of 2 production source files do not contain the fix's additive content.

Affected files (branch state):
- `dummyserver/app.py`
- `src/urllib3/response.py`

I'd appreciate confirmation on whether `1.26.x` is intentionally unpatched (EOL etc.) or whether a backport is planned. Happy to draft one if welcome.

Thanks!
— vulgraph

nodes.body:
Hi @vulgraph,

1.26.x is EOL and we do not backport fixes to it https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/policy#supported-versions

issues.title: Extract test dependency group, deduplicate dev and mypy
issues.body:
Closes #3594.

## Summary

Introduces a dedicated `test` dependency group containing only what is needed to run the test suite — no profiling (`coverage`, `pytest-memray`) and no maintainer tooling (`build`, `towncrier`). Downstream packagers (e.g. Fedora, see linked PR in the issue) can install just this group to generate build-time test requirements without patching the contents of `dev`.

`dev-base` now layers on top of `test` and adds the maintainer/profiling tools, so `dev` and `dev-min-pyopenssl` retain the same final dependency closure as before. `mypy` also includes `test` instead of repeating its contents, eliminating the duplication called out in the issue.

This implements @pquentin's suggestion in https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3594#issuecomment-2997196389:

> Sure, that sounds good, we can add a new group called `test` and include it in `dev` and `mypy`.

## Equivalence

I verified via `uv export --frozen --only-group <name> --no-hashes` that the resolved package set is **byte-for-byte identical** for `dev`, `dev-base`, and `dev-min-pyopenssl` before vs. after.

The `mypy` group additionally pulls `pysocks`, `pytest-socket`, and `pytest-timeout` (because they now come in via the shared `test` group). `nox -s mypy` still passes with no changes — the existing `# type: ignore[import-untyped]` annotations on the SOCKS imports cover them. Happy to split `mypy` back out from `test` if you'd prefer to keep its environment leaner.

## On `idna`

@pquentin asked in the issue whether `idna` is still needed. I checked: it is.

- `src/urllib3/util/url.py:333` does a conditional `import idna` (try/except `ImportError`); without the package, `_idna_encode` raises `LocationParseError`.
- `test/test_util.py` exercises both paths: `test_create_connection_with_valid_idna_labels` requires the package to be present, and `class TestUtilWithoutIdna` (line 1093) uses an `ImportBlocker("idna")` to verify the fallback when it's missing.

The other places that mention `idna` in the source (`connection.py`, `util/connection.py`) use Python's stdlib `encodings.idna` codec via `host.encode("idna")` and don't need the package. So `idna` stays in `dev`/`mypy`.

## Test plan

- [x] `nox -s mypy` — passes (83 files, no issues)
- [x] `nox -s lint` — passes
- [x] `uv lock --check` — clean after the refactor
- [x] `uv export` diff for `dev`/`dev-base`/`dev-min-pyopenssl`: identical closures
- [x] `pre-commit run` on touched files — passes
- [x] `towncrier check` — fragment found and renders correctly
- [ ] Full CI on push

issues.title: Sync test/port_helpers.py with CPython 3.14 socket_helper.py
issues.body:
Closes #3719.

## Summary

`test/port_helpers.py` was last copied from CPython 3.9's `Lib/test/support/socket_helper.py`. Per @Calvin0125's investigation in the issue, the only change in the two functions urllib3 uses (`find_unused_port` and `bind_port`) between CPython 3.9 and 3.14 is the Microsoft documentation URL in the `find_unused_port` docstring — the old `http://msdn2.microsoft.com/...` redirects to `https://learn.microsoft.com/...`.

This PR:

- Updates the URL.
- Bumps the source-version comment from "Python 3.9" to "Python 3.14".

## On Calvin's secondary question

> If the intention was to look through the urllib3 test suite and see if any of the new functions in `socket_helper.py` 3.14.0 would be useful…

I checked. The new additions in CPython 3.14 are `create_unix_domain_name()` (Unix-socket helper), `_get_sysctl()` and friends (read kernel sysctls on Linux/FreeBSD), and `has_gethostname` (a WASI capability flag). urllib3's test suite doesn't bind UNIX sockets, doesn't read sysctls, and targets Emscripten/Pyodide rather than WASI for its WebAssembly path — so nothing additional is worth importing today.

## Note on the dropped closing paren

CPython 3.14 also dropped the closing `)` from that same URL line, leaving the surrounding parenthetical block (started with `(This is easy to reproduce on Windows...`) unbalanced. I kept the `)` here to preserve a well-formed docstring. Happy to drop it if you'd prefer an exact byte-for-byte mirror of CPython 3.14.

## Test plan

- [x] `nox -s mypy` — passes (83 files, no issues)
- [x] `nox -s lint` — passes
- [x] `pre-commit run` on touched files — pyupgrade/black/isort/flake8 all pass
- [x] `towncrier check` — fragment found
- [ ] Full CI on push

Credit to @Calvin0125 for the upstream-diff investigation; he didn't end up submitting a PR, so picking it up here.

issues.title: Add cleartext HTTP/2 h2c support
issues.body:
Closes #3303.

## Summary

This adds explicit h2c support to the experimental HTTP/2 adapter.

Related: #5015 splits out the HTTP/2 socket reuse fix that this change depends
on. If that lands first, I can rebase this PR so the remaining diff stays
focused on h2c.

The existing `inject_into_urllib3()` behavior is unchanged: HTTPS pools still use
HTTP/2 and HTTP pools stay on HTTP/1.1 by default. Cleartext HTTP/2 has to be
enabled explicitly:

- `inject_into_urllib3(h2c=True)`
- `inject_into_urllib3(h2c="prior_knowledge")`
- `inject_into_urllib3(h2c="upgrade")`

The prior-knowledge path uses a cleartext `HTTPConnection` socket and starts the
HTTP/2 connection immediately. The upgrade path sends an HTTP/1.1
`Upgrade: h2c` request, waits for `101 Switching Protocols`, and then continues
the request as HTTP/2 on stream 1.

The cleartext connection also uses `:scheme` `http` and port `80` as the default
authority port.

Prior-knowledge h2c now opens the cleartext socket before sending HTTP/2 frames
through an `HTTPConnectionPool`. HTTP/2 connections also avoid the HTTP/1.1
dropped-connection probe, since a readable HTTP/2 socket can just have control
frames waiting and should still be reusable.

I also reset h2c upgrade state when an upgrade falls back to an HTTP/1.1
response or when the connection is closed, so a pooled connection does not carry
stale HTTP/2 state into a later request.

## Tests

Added coverage for:

- prior-knowledge cleartext requests;
- HTTP/1.1 upgrade request headers;
- switching to HTTP/2 after a `101` response;
- `HTTPConnectionPool` with `h2c=True` reusing one connection for two requests;
- `HTTPConnectionPool` with `h2c="upgrade"` reusing one connection for two requests;
- opt-in injection and restoration behavior;
- repeated injection and upgrade-state reset behavior.

I also added a changelog fragment.

## Local checks

- `uv run pytest test/test_http2_connection.py test/test_compatibility.py -q`
- `uv run pytest test/with_dummyserver/test_https.py -q -k "http2 or alpn or simple"`
- `uv run pytest test/with_dummyserver/test_connectionpool.py -q -k "http2"`

issues.title: Keep HTTP/2 sockets reusable with pending control frames
issues.body:
Closes #3301.

## Summary

HTTP/2 sockets can be readable even when the connection is still healthy. For
example, the peer may have sent a control frame after the response stream ended.
The HTTP/1.1 dropped-connection probe treats any readable socket as disconnected,
which can cause a pooled `HTTP2Connection` to be closed instead of reused.

This is also split out from #5014 so the socket reuse behavior can be reviewed
independently from h2c support.

This overrides `HTTP2Connection.is_connected` so the pool keeps an open HTTP/2
socket available for future requests. The existing request model is unchanged:
urllib3 still has one active request per pooled connection here, and this does
not add HTTP/2 multiplexing.

## Tests

Added a socketpair regression test that:

- sends a complete HTTP/2 response;
- leaves a pending HTTP/2 control frame on the socket;
- returns the connection to an `HTTPSConnectionPool`;
- checks that the same connection is reused without closing the socket;
- sends a second request on the reused HTTP/2 connection and reads the response.

## Local checks

issues.title: Unfold obsolete folded response header values
issues.body:
Addresses the original obs-fold response-header case discussed in #1362.

Python's `http.client` preserves obsolete folded response header lines in
`HTTPMessage` values. This change replaces each RFC 9112
`OWS CRLF RWS` sequence with a single space before urllib3 or downstream
consumers interpret the value.

The normalization:

- keeps urllib3's `HTTPHeaderDict` and the original `HTTPMessage` synchronized,
  preventing cookie consumers such as Requests from re-emitting raw CRLF;
- preserves header names, ordering, duplicate fields, and parser state;
- uses a common-case fast path and a linear-time pattern for long field values.

The socket regression covers the original folded `Set-Cookie`, duplicate
cookies, every SP/HTAB combination around CRLF, mixed and repeated whitespace,
multiple folds, and ordinary headers. Focused unit coverage also verifies
adjacent folds and preservation of the original message's order, duplicates,
payload, policy, and defects.

This intentionally does not address the separate whitespace-before-colon/header
name validation scope discussed on #1362.

Validation performed:

- full local suite: 2,279 passed, 333 skipped, 4 xfailed;
- focused strict nox sessions on Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14;
- pyupgrade, Black, isort, and flake8;
- towncrier changelog validation;
- source distribution and wheel builds;
- end-to-end Requests cookie extraction and subsequent request serialization.

nodes.body:
Small scope clarification after re-reading #1362 and the newer related PRs:

This PR is intentionally limited to the original obs-folded response-header value case from the issue body. It does not attempt to fix the later/current whitespace-before-colon header-name scope, which #5013 is already addressing.

I also noticed #5017 covers a very similar obs-fold normalization path and was opened earlier. I am happy to close this in favor of #5017, or keep it open only if maintainers prefer this smaller diff/test shape.
Thanks @sethmlarson, I appreciate you reviewing the competing approaches and keeping this PR open.

Pushed `00162b20`, rebased onto current `main`, and addressed all four review
threads.

Two additional issues surfaced during end-to-end and adversarial validation:

1. Normalizing only `HTTPHeaderDict` left the original #1362 Requests
   reproduction intact because Requests extracts cookies from
   `response._original_response.msg`. The implementation now updates that same
   `HTTPMessage` in place only when a fold is found, preserving its identity,
   parser state, global header order, and duplicates.
2. The literal `[ \t]*\r\n[ \t]+` suggestion has quadratic behavior on long
   whitespace runs. The committed expression is substitution-equivalent but
   linear-time; exhaustive small-input and randomized equivalence checks include
   adjacent and repeated folds.

﻿## Summary

This normalizes obsolete folded response header values before urllib3 exposes them through `HTTPHeaderDict`. ## What changed

This PR teaches `ProxyManager` to derive `Proxy-Authorization` from credentials embedded in the proxy URL when explicit `proxy_headers` do not already provide it.

`ProxyManager("http://user:pass@host:port")` previously parsed the credentials but did not send them as a `Proxy-Authorization` header, so authenticated proxy URLs did not work as expected.

Users can now pass proxy credentials directly in the proxy URL and have them sent to the proxy on the first request.

issues.title: Resolve connection pool queue class lazily
issues.body:
This PR resolves #3289 by deferring resolution of the default connection-pool queue class until a pool is constructed.

Previously `ConnectionPool.QueueCls` captured `queue.LifoQueue` at import time. If a runtime such as gevent patched the `queue` module after urllib3 was imported, the default pool still used the original class reference. The change keeps custom `QueueCls` subclasses working as before, but when the class is still the default it uses the current `queue.LifoQueue` at pool creation time.

issues.title: fix: do not mutate caller-supplied proxy_ssl_context verify_mode
issues.body:
## Summary

Fixes #4961.

When `_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname` received a user-provided `ssl_context` it unconditionally overwrote `context.verify_mode` with the *target* connection's `cert_reqs` value. Two problems:

1. **`_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname`** set `context.verify_mode` regardless of whether the context was created internally or supplied by the caller. User-provided contexts must not be mutated.

2. **`_connect_tls_proxy`** forwarded `self.cert_reqs` (the *target's* `cert_reqs`) to the proxy TLS handshake. When `cert_reqs='CERT_NONE'` was set for the target this leaked into the proxy path and, via problem 1, permanently downgraded the proxy's SSL verification level.

## Changes

- `_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname`: guard the `verify_mode` assignment behind `if default_ssl_context` so caller-supplied contexts are left unmodified.
- `_connect_tls_proxy`: pass `cert_reqs=None` so the proxy TLS handshake respects the `proxy_ssl_context`'s own `verify_mode` (or defaults to `CERT_REQUIRED` for newly-created contexts).
- Added a unit test in `test_ssl.py` that verifies `verify_mode` is not mutated on a user-supplied context.

## Checklist

- [x] Changes are covered by tests
- [x] `changelog/4961.bugfix.rst` added
- [x] No breaking changes — callers who relied on the (broken) leaking behaviour would have been silently weakening proxy TLS verification

issues.title: Confusing FullPoolError raised when passing a string timeout
issues.body:
### Subject

In general, urllib3 validates that timeouts are ints or floats, and raises a meaningful exception when this isn't the case. Example:

```python
r = urllib3.request("GET", "http://localhost:9200/", timeout="1")
```

Which raises:

```
ValueError: Timeout value connect was 1, but it must be an int, float or None.
```
But we have found one instance where instead we are seeing an obscure seemingly unrelated exception:

```python
pool = urllib3.HTTPConnectionPool('localhost', 9200, block=True)
pool.urlopen('GET', "/", timeout="1")
```

Which raises:

```
urllib3.exceptions.FullPoolError: HTTPConnectionPool(host='localhost', port=9200): Pool reached maximum size and no more connections are allowed.
```

### Environment

OS macOS-26.5-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
Python 3.14.3
OpenSSL 3.5.5 27 Jan 2026
urllib3 2.6.3

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import urllib3

pool = urllib3.HTTPConnectionPool('localhost', 9200, block=True)
pool.urlopen('GET', "/", timeout="1")
```

### Expected Behavior

A `ValueError` is raised.

### Actual Behavior

A `FullPoolError` is raised.

nodes.body: We pass that to https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/29ae1419530857dc43f5d28907da5d6fbc229739/src/urllib3/connectionpool.py#L346-L356 which falls back to https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/29ae1419530857dc43f5d28907da5d6fbc229739/src/urllib3/util/timeout.py#L173-L186 assuming the value is a float. `float("1")`. Is a valid float but we don't return it here: https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/29ae1419530857dc43f5d28907da5d6fbc229739/src/urllib3/util/timeout.py#L150-L170 so I'd suggest a `value = float("1")` in the first try/except to solve this
Thanks! ❤️

issues.title: Fix port-zero handling
issues.body:
@christos-spearbit noticed that previously, when a new request passed `port=0`, pool selection treated that value as if no port had been provided at all, so it fell back to the scheme default (80 for HTTP or 443 for HTTPS) and reused the existing default-port pool instead of creating or selecting a distinct port-zero pool.

This change preserves port 0 as a distinct one in URL parsing, pool selection, and proxy configuration.

nodes.body:
@sigmavirus24 that's a good question!

My primary goal is to ensure that if a user explicitly requests port 0, urllib3 does not implicitly fall back to port 80 or 443.

While browsers like Firefox and Chrome block requests to port 0, curl will attempt the connection (as detailed in [Daniel's blog post](https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2014/10/25/pretending-port-zero-is-a-normal-one/)).

Personally, I think it's best to let the underlying operating system decide how to handle a port 0 request rather than blocking it at the library level. However, I'm indifferent to the exact behavior as long as we stop defaulting it to port 80/443.

issues.title: `SSL_KEYWORDS` is missing `assert_hostname` and `assert_fingerprint`, leaking HTTPS-only kwargs into HTTP connection construction
issues.body:
### Subject

`PoolManager._new_pool` strips SSL-only kwargs from connection-pool
kwargs when creating an HTTP pool, via the `SSL_KEYWORDS` allowlist.
That list is missing `assert_hostname` and `assert_fingerprint`, both
of which are HTTPS-only (declared as named parameters on
`HTTPSConnection.__init__`, rejected by `HTTPConnection.__init__`).

When a caller sets either on `PoolManager.connection_pool_kw` and then
issues a plain-HTTP request, the kwarg leaks past the filter into
`HTTPConnection.__init__`, which raises a `TypeError`.

Adding both to `SSL_KEYWORDS` fixes it, matching the existing intent
of the filter.

### Environment


```python
>>> OS macOS-26.3.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
>>> Python 3.14.5
>>> OpenSSL 3.6.2 7 Apr 2026
>>> urllib3 2.7.0
```

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import urllib3


def show(kwarg: str) -> None:
    pool = urllib3.PoolManager()
    pool.connection_pool_kw[kwarg] = False
    print(f"--- connection_pool_kw[{kwarg!r}] = False, GET http://...")
    try:
        pool.request("GET", "http://127.0.0.1:1/", retries=False, timeout=0.1)
    except TypeError as exc:
        print(f"  TypeError: {exc}")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"  {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
    print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"urllib3 version: {urllib3.__version__}\n")
    # Both leak; both should be in SSL_KEYWORDS.
    show("assert_hostname")
    show("assert_fingerprint")

    # For contrast: cert_reqs IS in SSL_KEYWORDS, gets stripped correctly.
    show("cert_reqs")
```

### Expected Behavior

A `PoolManager` with `assert_hostname` or `assert_fingerprint` set on
`connection_pool_kw` should successfully dispatch to plain-HTTP URLs.
Those kwargs should be stripped before reaching
`HTTPConnection.__init__`, the same way `cert_reqs`, `ca_certs`, and
the rest of `SSL_KEYWORDS` already are.

### Actual Behavior

`HTTPConnection.__init__` raises `TypeError`:

```
TypeError: HTTPConnection.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assert_hostname'
```

The same happens for `assert_fingerprint`. For comparison, kwargs
already in `SSL_KEYWORDS` (e.g. `cert_reqs`) are correctly stripped
and the request proceeds to the network leg.


```
--- connection_pool_kw['assert_hostname'] = False, GET http://...
  TypeError: HTTPConnection.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assert_hostname'

--- connection_pool_kw['assert_fingerprint'] = False, GET http://...
  TypeError: HTTPConnection.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assert_fingerprint'

--- connection_pool_kw['cert_reqs'] = False, GET http://...
  NewConnectionError: HTTPConnection(host='127.0.0.1', port=1): Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 61] Connection refused
```

issues.title: Strip fragments from absolute request targets
issues.body:
urllib3 could send URL fragments in absolute-form request targets for HTTPConnectionPool absolute URLs/absolute redirects and proxied HTTP requests, potentially leaking client-side fragment data to origin servers or proxies.

Relevant excerpts from the RFCs
> [3.2.2. ](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9112#section-3.2.2)[absolute-form](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9112#name-absolute-form)
When making a request to a proxy, other than a CONNECT or server-wide OPTIONS request (as detailed below), a client MUST send the target URI in "absolute-form" as the request-target.
>  absolute-form  = absolute-URI

> [4.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-4.3).  Absolute URI
>   Some protocol elements allow only the absolute form of a URI without
>   a fragment identifier.  For example, defining a base URI for later
>   use by relative references calls for an absolute-URI syntax rule that
>   does not allow a fragment.
>   absolute-URI  = scheme ":" hier-part [ "?" query ]

issues.title: reject control characters and spaces in URL host in parse_url
issues.body:
1. `parse_url` percent-encodes control characters in the userinfo, path, query, and fragment components (`test_control_characters_are_percent_encoded` pins this), but the host was returned verbatim, so a host containing a control character or space, including CR and LF, passed through the parser unchanged. `_REG_NAME_PAT` only excludes `[ ] % : / ? #`, so the bytes `0x00-0x20` and `0x7f` survive.
2. Reject a host containing any of those characters with `LocationParseError` in `parse_url`, the single parsing chokepoint that `is_same_host` and the proxy/pool paths also go through. The character set matches `http.client._contains_disallowed_url_pchar_re`, keeping the parser at least as strict as the stdlib transport the host is handed to, and keeping host-based caller checks from receiving a malformed host.

Validation: `parse_url("http://exa\r\nmple.com/")` previously returned `host=exa
mple.com`; it now raises `LocationParseError`. Added `test_control_characters_in_host_are_rejected` over the same character range as the existing percent-encoding test (fails before the change, passes after). Existing url and pool tests still pass.

issues.title: Include explicit port 0 in Url.netloc and Url.authority
issues.body:
## Problem

`Url.netloc` (and `Url.authority`, which builds on it) silently drops an explicit
port `0`, because it uses a truthiness check:

```python
# src/urllib3/util/url.py
if self.port:
    return f"{self.host}:{self.port}"
return self.host
```

`0` is falsy, so a parsed `:0` is omitted. This contradicts:

- the sibling `url` property, which uses `if port is not None:` and explicitly
  documents the intent — *"We use 'is not None' [because] we want things to
  happen with empty strings (or 0 port)"*; and
- the stdlib-parity contract asserted by the existing
  `test_authority_matches_urllib_netloc`, since `urlparse("http://h:0/").netloc`
  keeps `"h:0"`.

`parse_url` already accepts `:0` (`_HOST_PORT_RE` matches it and sets
`.port == 0`), so this is reachable:

```python
>>> parse_url("http://example.com:0/path").url
'http://example.com:0/path'
>>> parse_url("http://example.com:0/path").netloc
'example.com'                     # bug: expected 'example.com:0'
>>> parse_url("http://u:p@example.com:0/path").authority
'u:p@example.com'                 # bug: expected 'u:p@example.com:0'
```

## Fix

Use `if self.port is not None:` in `netloc`, matching the `url` property and
stdlib behaviour.

## Tests

Added `:0` cases to the existing `url_authority_map` and `url_netloc_map`
parametrizations in `test/test_util.py`. They fail on `main`
(`test_netloc`/`test_authority` return the port-less form) and pass with the
fix; `test_authority_matches_urllib_netloc` confirms the expected values match
`urlparse().netloc`. `black`/`isort` clean.

issues.title: Fix: treat empty allowed_methods as retrying no methods
issues.body:
## Description

An empty container for `allowed_methods` (e.g., `set()`) was previously treated the same as `None`, allowing retries on **all** HTTP methods. This is error-prone because users can accidentally produce an empty set (e.g., using `&` instead of `|` when combining allowed methods) without realizing the retry behavior is incorrect.

This fix changes the behavior so that an empty `allowed_methods` container means **no** methods are retryable, matching the intuitive expectation.

## Changes

- `src/urllib3/util/retry.py`: Changed `_is_method_retryable` to use `is not None` instead of truthiness check

## Testing

- `None` → all methods retryable (unchanged)
- `set()` → no methods retryable (fixed)
- `{"GET"}` → only GET retryable (unchanged)

Fixes #5044

nodes.body:
Drive-by: the `lint` failure here is two `mypy` errors, and both are one-line annotations. Posting the diff rather than a suggestion box since they are in two different files.

```
src/urllib3/connection.py:901: error: Incompatible types in assignment
    (expression has type "SSLContext | None", variable has type "SSLContext")  [assignment]
test/with_dummyserver/test_proxy_poolmanager.py:833: error: Item "None" of
    "ProxyConfig | None" has no attribute "ssl_context"  [union-attr]
```

**First one** — in `_connect_tls_proxy`, `ssl_context` is inferred as `SSLContext` from the `if` branch, then the `else` branch can assign `None`:

```python
ssl_context = self.ssl_context if self.proxy_is_forwarding else None
```

`cert_reqs` right below it already declares its union up front, so the fix matches the surrounding style:

```diff
+        ssl_context: ssl.SSLContext | None
         cert_reqs: int | str | None
         if proxy_ssl_context is not None:
```

**Second one** — `proxy_config` is `ProxyConfig | None`, and `proxy_from_url(...)` always sets it, so narrowing is enough:

```diff
         assert proxy.proxy_ssl_context is ssl_context
+        assert proxy.proxy_config is not None
         assert proxy.proxy_config.ssl_context is None
```

With both applied on your branch (`f1ea8b14`):

```
$ mypy -p urllib3    # connection.py: no errors
$ mypy -p test       # test_proxy_poolmanager.py: no errors
```

Two things I checked so this is not misleading:

- **The `coverage` failure is separate** and I have not looked at it; this only addresses `lint`.
- `black --check` also flags `connection.py`, but the diff is at lines 270/312 (`(version, code, message)` → `version, code, message`), which is **pre-existing and unrelated to this PR** — my local black is simply a different version than CI's. I left it alone.

Happy to open this as a PR against your branch if that is easier than applying it by hand.

Drive-by: the only red check here is `changelog entry`, and it is a missing file rather than anything wrong with the change. Since you are packaging this downstream rather than working in this repo day to day, here is the exact shape it wants.

Naming is `<ISSUE-OR-PR>.<TYPE>.rst`; `changelog/README.rst` says to use the issue number if there is one, and the PR number otherwise, which is `5097` here. Types are the five towncrier defaults — `bugfix` is the right one for this.

There is also an escape hatch if the maintainers would rather not spend a line on it: the workflow passes when the **`Skip Changelog`** label is applied. That is a maintainer action, not something you can set yourself, but worth knowing it exists.

issues.title: Preserve explicit port 0 in connection_from_url and HTTP/2 authority
issues.body: connection_from_url() and the HTTP/2 request authority build the port with a truthiness check, so an explicit :0 in the URL gets dropped and replaced by the default 80 or 443. This is the same handling #5071 corrected for URL parsing, pool selection, and proxy configuration, but these two call sites were left using `port or <default>`. Switching them to an explicit None check keeps an explicit port 0.

issues.title: Add assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint to SSL_KEYWORDS
issues.body:
## Summary

Adds `assert_hostname` and `assert_fingerprint` to the `SSL_KEYWORDS` allowlist so they are properly stripped when constructing HTTP (non-HTTPS) connection pools.

Fixes #5077

## Problem

When a caller sets `assert_hostname` or `assert_fingerprint` on `PoolManager.connection_pool_kw` and then issues a plain-HTTP request, the kwarg leaks past the `SSL_KEYWORDS` filter into `HTTPConnection.__init__`, which raises a `TypeError`.

## Fix

Add both to `SSL_KEYWORDS`, matching the existing intent of the filter.

## Verification

- Reproduced the issue with the reproducer from the issue report.
- Verified the fix: with the change, both kwargs are correctly stripped before reaching `HTTPConnection.__init__`.

## Disclosure

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); I reviewed and verified the change and test results, and will respond to review feedback personally.
